Team —

Quick sync item for today's planning: Orbis Analytics is requesting a 6-week pilot starting the week of Mar 18 that will need a mix of steady reserved capacity plus short daily "burst slots" in the evenings for load testing. They expect peak concurrent inference to hit ~220k tokens/min during tests.

Ask: can infra commit a conservative reserve and carve out 40 burst slots (A100-equivalent) for the pilot window? Finance/sales, I need a sketch of committed hours and uplift discount we can offer for a 6-week pilot convertible to Dedicated in Q3.

Attachments: pipeline_forecast_Q2.xlsx (forecast from sales), I pasted the HubSpot link below.

Please reply with two things by EOD: 1) a capacity delta we can hold aside from the current reservations, and 2) a rough $/hour uplift cost for burst usage (so we can propose a sensible burn rate to the customer).

Thanks —
Ben

Ben / all —

We ran a quick check against the current reservation calendar and the forecasted renewals. Short answer: we can free up 28 A100-equivalent slots from the general pool for Mar 18–Apr 29 if we shift two low-priority canaries (ETA for reschedule: +2 weeks) and lean on burstable instances for the nightly runs. If we also use quantized variants for the test sequences, effective capacity jumps another ~10% (so roughly equivalent to 31 slots).

Notes: 1) Those 28 slots assume no simultaneous large batch runs from Nimbus (their renewal slated for Mar 22) — if Nimbus runs heavy, we need to re-evaluate.
2) Network egress for their test windows will need traffic shaping; ops will need to pre-configure rate limits to protect cross-tenant QoS.

I'll attach a small calc file for the slot/time breakdown (capacity_calc_q2.csv). We should talk about whether the customer needs strict Dedicated isolation vs. soft-reserved slots.

Ben / team / Tom —

Quick cost sketch from Finance: for a 6-week pilot with a convertible clause, we can offer a pilot uplift rate of $2.30/hr per A100-equivalent for burst hours (peak window), and $1.35/hr for steady reserved pilot capacity (non-peak). If Orbis signs a Q3 Dedicated commitment (>=3 months) we can credit 30% of pilot spend against the first-month fee.

Assumptions: 28 reserved slots for steady usage, plus 14 additional burstable slots (we're trying to be conservative given Laura's note). If Tom's team needs the full 40 burst slots we should treat 12 of those as billed at a premium one-time burst premium ($2.75/hr) unless we reallocate more from the pool.

I've attached capacity_calc_q2.csv which shows a couple of scenarios (28 steady + 14 burst vs 31 steady-equivalent via quantization). Also added a quick MOP for fallback: auto-route to quantized variant (same model family) with a soft SLA on latency degradation up to 15%.

Aditya Rao
Sr. Finance Analyst, GTM Economics
Redwood Inference

- Capacity: conservatively hold 28 A100-equivalent steady slots (Mar 18–Apr 29) and provision 14 burstable slots for evening tests (total effective capacity if quantized ~= 31 slots).
- Pricing: pilot uplift = $2.30/hr (burst), $1.35/hr (steady). If Orbis converts to Dedicated in Q3 we credit 30% of pilot spend. If customer requires all 40 burst slots as Dedicated for the pilot, finance flags a $2.75/hr premium for the 12 oversubscribed slots.
- Fallback: auto-fallback to quantized variant w/ soft SLA (latency degrade <=15% during fallback).

Action items (owners):
- Laura: reserve the 28 steady slots and configure network QoS + rate limits by Mar 11. Attach: mutual_action_plan_Orbis.pdf (Miro of schedule + runbook)
- Aditya: finalize pilot pricing and write an addendum for the convertible credit (track in HubSpot deal).
- Karthik: pre-approve the infra changes and the burst policy; confirm whether we need a temporary capacity boost from Dedicated pool.
- Ben: draft the pilot SOW and send to Tom + procurement by EOD tomorrow.

Tom / procurement: we'll send the SOW and a simple PO flow once Aditya's addendum is in place. If you prefer a Dedicated wager for the pilot let us know and we'll price it out with the premium.
